title: Reduction of the recollement connecting map
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$, $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ closed and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open. Use the small pro-etale operation datum [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ in the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Put $K_n=r_nK$, where $r_n=-\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction].

Let $\varepsilon_K:j_!j^*K\to K$ be the counit of $j_!\dashv j^*$ and $\eta_K:K\to i_*i^*K$ the unit of $i^*\dashv i_*$ for the integral operations of the datum, and let $\delta_K:i_*i^*K\to j_!j^*K[1]$ be any morphism such that $\Delta_K=(j_!j^*K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_K}K\xrightarrow{\eta_K}i_*i^*K\xrightarrow{\delta_K}j_!j^*K[1])$ is a distinguished triangle in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R)$. Since $K_n\in D^b_c(X,A_n)$, let $\delta_{K_n}$ be any open--closed recollement triangle for $K_n$ in the sense of [def-weil-open-closed-recollement], and write $\Delta_{K_n}$ for the resulting distinguished triangle with the finite counit $\varepsilon_{K_n}$ and unit $\eta_{K_n}$. Let $a_n:r_n(j_!j^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!j^*K_n$ and $b_n:r_n(i_*i^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_*i^*K_n$ be the specified operation reduction comparisons [lem-fix-operation-reduction], and $s_n:r_n(M[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}(r_nM)[1]$ the derived-tensor shift comparison [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Then $(a_n,1_{K_n},b_n)$ is an isomorphism of distinguished triangles $r_n\Delta_K\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_{K_n}$ in the derived category. In particular its third square is the equality
$$a_n[1]\,s_n\,r_n(\delta_K)=\delta_{K_n}\,b_n.$$
This is natural in $K$ for the specified comparisons, and includes empty $U$ or $Z$.

proof.text: Apply the counit-normalized derived scalar-extension shift theorem to the coefficient projection. Uniqueness of its degree-one comparison identifies it with PurCompactSupport.scalarCommShift. Transport this coherent shift and exactness along finiteReductionIso. Thus the actual reduced integral triangle, with exactly the shift structure in sfRecollementReducedTriangle, is distinguished.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; counit normalization of the exact derived coefficient functor

proof.text: Read the open counit and closed unit equations from the reduction comparison of the supplied operation datum. For the open equation, use openAdjunction_left and openAdjunction_right, then cancel the inverse open comparison. Apply the finite ambient inclusion and its composition law. The results are precisely the first and second squares with vertex maps a_n, identity, b_n.

source.place: Clause (3), exact image of open-closed recollement, with the coefficient and adjunction comparisons specified by the operation datum

proof.text: The reduced input belongs to the finite constructible category by the definition of sixFunctorIntegralReduction. Apply the finite all-stages recollement theorem. Its shifted orthogonality concerns the canonical ordinary finite vertices. Identify the datum vertices with these vertices using finiteOpenExtension and finiteDirectImage followed by those functors applied to finitePullback. Transport the Hom subsingleton along these vertex isomorphisms, and then along a_n[1], to obtain Hom((r_n j!j*K)[1], i*i*K_n)=0. The coefficient prime is a unit in the closure field because its prime differs from the characteristic.

source.place: Hom vanishing paragraph, applied to the finite stage

proof.text: Apply triangle_morphism_extension, part (2), to the reduced integral and chosen finite distinguished triangles, with middle map identity and the prescribed outer maps a_n and b_n. The Hom subsingleton and the first two squares give the third square for these very maps. Triangle.isoMk packages their three component isomorphisms as an isomorphism of triangles. Its components are definitionally the prescribed maps. Unfold the third square and reassociate composition to obtain the displayed boundary equation. This avoids introducing a separate transported connecting arrow and then identifying it by uniqueness.

source.place: Corollaire 1.1.10(ii), as formalized by triangle_morphism_extension; the same vanishing and uniqueness argument as the node original steps 3--4

proof.text: For naturality, assemble each specified comparison into a natural isomorphism by whiskering its two factors with the operation functors and ambient inclusion. Their components are definitionally sfRecollementReductionOpenIso and sfRecollementReductionClosedIso. Apply the naturality equation of each composite. No step assumes a stratum nonempty, so the same argument includes empty U or Z.

I read the item and every cited statement in full. Step 1: lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings(2) gives exact Lπ_n^* = r_n, whose shift structure is s_n; Stacks 06YY was checked at sites-cohomology.tex:3585. Step 2: lem-fix-operation-reduction covers O_E→A_n reduction for pullback, direct image and compact-support image on the bounded domains, and its last clause preserves the j_!⊣j^* counit and i^*⊣i_* unit; this gives r_n(ε)=ε_n a_n and b_n r_n(η)=η_n. Step 3: δ̃=a_n[1]d b_n^{-1} gives a triangle iso, distinguished by TR1; checked against def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift. Step 4: the finite-stage clause of prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages gives Hom(j_!j^*K_n[m],i_*i^*K_n)=0 and a unique third arrow, in the right direction (BBD 1.1.10(ii)); so δ̃=δ_{K_n}, and right-composing with b_n gives the displayed equality. Step 5: componentwise naturality. Empty X/U/Z and n=1 were checked. The integral-to-finite coefficient categories match the parent's use and are at least as general as it needs. lean.statement: theorem sfRecollementReductionBoundary [IsSeparated X.obj.hom] [IsClosedImmersion i.hom.left] (_hij : Set.range j.hom.left.base = (Set.range i.hom.left.base)ᶜ) (m : ℕ) (K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory C.l E X.obj.left) (δ : (sfReductionIntegralClosed S i).obj K ⟶ ((sfReductionIntegralOpen S j hj).obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) (_hδ : sfReductionIntegralTriangle S i j hj K δ ∈ distTriang _) (δn : (sfReductionFiniteClosed S i m).obj K ⟶ ((sfReductionFiniteOpen S j hj m).obj K)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧) (_hδn : sfReductionFiniteTriangle S i j hj m K δn ∈ distTriang _) : (∃ e : sfRecollementReducedTriangle (C := C) (E := E) (X := X) m (sfReductionIntegralTriangle S i j hj K δ) ≅ sfReductionFiniteTriangle S i j hj m K δn, e.hom.hom₁ = (sfRecollementReductionOpenIso S j hj m K).hom ∧ e.hom.hom₂ = 𝟙 _ ∧ e.hom.hom₃ = (sfRecollementReductionClosedIso S i m K).hom) ∧ (scalarReductionDerivedExtension C.l E X.obj.left m).map δ ≫ (Functor.commShiftIso (scalarReductionDerivedExtension C.l E X.obj.left m) (self := Functor.CommShift.ofIso (PurCompactSupport.finiteReductionIso C.l E X.obj.left m) ℤ) (1 : ℤ)).hom.app ((sfReductionIntegralOpen S j hj).obj K) ≫ (shiftFunctor _ (1 : ℤ)).map (sfRecollementReductionOpenIso S j hj m K).hom = (sfRecollementReductionClosedIso S i m K).hom ≫ δn
lean.note: The main theorem gives the prescribed triangle isomorphism and its boundary equation in the ambient derived category; the second theorem states its componentwise naturality. Helpers only compose the recorded operation functors, adjunction maps, ambient inclusions and reduction comparisons. All positive levels use exponent m+1.
